remember.question: Define the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model and list all seven layers in their hierarchical order from lowest to highest, stating the fundamental responsibility of each layer.
State the core definition of symmetric-key cryptography. List any four standard symmetric cipher algorithms and identify the key sizes supported by AES.
Define connection establishment in TCP. List the sequence of control flags (SYN, ACK) exchanged during the 3-way handshake process and identify the socket states.

understand.question: Explain the working mechanism of the Distance Vector Routing algorithm using the Bellman-Ford equation. Describe the count-to-infinity problem and how split horizon with poison reverse mitigates it.
Describe the difference between stemming and lemmatization in natural language preprocessing. Explain how morphological analysis using WordNet produces linguistically valid root forms.
Discuss in detail the four interdependent congestion control mechanisms employed by TCP: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery. Provide a neat cwnd versus time graph.

apply.question: Solve the single-source shortest path problem for a given weighted network topology with 6 nodes (A through F). Illustrate each step in a tabular trace showing tentative distances and permanent labels.
Demonstrate the RSA encryption and decryption mechanism. Given prime numbers p = 11, q = 13, and encryption key e = 7, compute the private key d and encrypt the plaintext message M = 9.

Apply Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) principles to divide the IP address block 192.168.10.0/24 into four equal subnets. Calculate the subnet mask, network address, broadcast address, and usable host range for each subnet.

analyze.question: Differentiate between TCP and UDP protocols based on connection state, error recovery, flow control, and transmission overhead. Compare their suitability for real-time video conferencing versus critical financial data transfer.

analyze.subtopic: Dense Semantic Embeddings vs Sparse TF-IDF
analyze.question: Compare dense semantic vector embeddings (Sentence-BERT) with sparse lexical representations (TF-IDF) in information retrieval. Analyze their computational complexity, vocabulary mismatch limitations, and performance on out-of-vocabulary words.

Analyze the structural differences between IPv4 and IPv6 packet headers. Contrast how fragmentation, checksum verification, and option handling are implemented in each architecture to improve routing efficiency.

evaluate.subtopic: Public Key Infrastructure and Digital Certificates
evaluate.question: Critique the security vulnerabilities inherent in centralized Certificate Authority (CA) architectures. Justify whether decentralized trust models, such as Web of Trust or blockchain-anchored PKI, provide superior resilience against man-in-the-middle attacks.

evaluate.subtopic: Stop-and-Wait vs Sliding Window Flow Control
evaluate.question: Evaluate the channel utilization efficiency of the Stop-and-Wait protocol compared to Go-Back-N and Selective Repeat sliding window protocols over a high-bandwidth satellite link. Justify your conclusion with mathematical throughput derivations.

evaluate.subtopic: Dense Vector Search vs Hybrid Lexical-Neural Retrieval
evaluate.question: Assess the limitations of relying purely on dense vector similarity search (FAISS IndexFlatIP) for technical curriculum domains. Justify whether a hybrid retrieval pipeline combining reciprocal rank fusion with BM25 yields superior retrieval precision.

create.question: Design an end-to-end multi-tier network security architecture for a university campus intranet. Formulate the firewall rules, demilitarized zone (DMZ) placement, VPN gateway, and intrusion detection system (IDS) topology with a comprehensive architectural diagram.

Formulate the complete architectural pipeline of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system for automated examination paper synthesis. Design the document ingestion, sentence-aware chunking, vector indexing, contextual prompt formatting, and multi-metric evaluation subsystems.

Design a lightweight consensus algorithm suitable for resource-constrained IoT mesh networks. Formulate the state transition diagram, leader election mechanism, and message exchange protocol to achieve Byzantine fault tolerance.
